narrative: This collection agency calls me 4 to 5 times a day, sometimes before 8am, about a payday loan debt. I have asked them multiple times to only contact me by mail and they keep calling anyway. It's gotten to the point where I'm afraid to answer my phone.
extracted_allegations: Collection agency calls 4 to 5 times a day about a payday loan debt | Some calls occur before 8am | Customer asked multiple times to be contacted only by mail and the agency continues to call
policy_cited: 08 General Dispute Handling Process, Standard process and 'What counts as a complete response' (with Policy 10 Prohibited Language and Policy 11 Response Tone and Format)
draft_text:
You told us a collection agency has been calling you four to five times a day about a payday loan, that some of the calls come before 8am, and that you've asked several times to be contacted only by mail but the calls haven't stopped. Being called that often and that early, after you've asked for something different, is stressful, and we want to go through each part with you.

The number of calls: Our call records back this up. They show 4 calls on March 30 and 5 calls on March 31, so 9 calls in two days.

The early calls: Our records show calls at 7:41am on March 30 and 7:55am on March 31. They don't show a time zone, so we can't tell from them what time it was where you are. If you let us know your local time for those calls, we'll add that to your case.

Your requests for mail-only contact: We couldn't confirm this part. Your account notes don't contain a mail-only request, and the call records we have start on March 30. That means we can't see when or how you asked, or whether the agency received your request. It doesn't mean you didn't ask. It means we don't have a record of it.

What happens next: You asked to be contacted by mail only. That request, along with the call details above, has been referred for review. We can't confirm an outcome yet, so please don't treat mail-only contact as in place.

If you can, please reply with the dates and the way you asked for mail-only contact (for example by phone or in writing), and the local time of the early calls. You're welcome to send us anything else at any time, and we'll review it. You're also free to raise your concerns through any other channel you choose.

Case reference: 20962593
action_required_before_sending: The customer's request for mail-only contact, plus the confirmed call-frequency and before-8am call details, is referred for review. The reviewer should make this referral before the draft is sent. The draft promises no outcome.

A $35 late fee was then charged on April 15th, and your payment was recorded on your account that same day. Our records confirm the payment reached us before the due date and that the late fee was charged anyway.

The mobile app payment: This part of your account of events matches what we have. Our records show the payment was made through the mobile app on April 13th. We don't have your screenshot on file, but we didn't need it to confirm the payment.

What happens next: We've referred the $35 late fee for approval to have it corrected. We can't tell you the outcome or timing yet, because that depends on the approval. If you have anything else you'd like us to look at, including the screenshot, you can send it any time and we'll review it. You can also reply to this message or call the number on your account to ask where things stand.

narrative: My payment this month was taken out twice from my bank account, for $220 total instead of $110. This has caused an overdraft on my checking account.
extracted_allegations: Monthly payment was taken out twice from bank account, totaling $220 instead of $110 | Double payment caused an overdraft on checking account
policy_cited: 08 General Dispute Handling Process (standard process: respond to every allegation individually, state a clear next step); Policy 10 Prohibited Language and Policy 11 Response Tone and Format applied
draft_text:

The double payment: Our records confirm your payment was taken twice. We took one payment of $110 on June 30 and a second payment of $110 on July 1, which comes to $220 against the $110 you expected.

The refund: Because our records confirm the second payment, we've referred the refund of it for approval. We can't promise the outcome or timing yet, but once that review is finished we'll write to you with the result.

The overdraft: We can't see an overdraft fee on your account with us. Any overdraft on your checking account would have been recorded by your bank, so our records can't confirm it or rule it out. This doesn't mean we doubt what you've told us. If you'd like us to look at it, you're welcome to send a copy of the bank statement or notice showing the overdraft and any fees. We'll review whatever you send.

Next steps: You don't need to do anything for the refund review. If you have anything else you'd like us to consider, you can send it at any time by replying to this message or calling the number on your account, and we'll review it. Your case reference number is SYN-P02. Please include it in any further correspondence.
action_required_before_sending: Refund of the duplicate $110 payment (taken July 1, 2026) has been referred for approval; the reviewer should submit this referral before the draft is sent.
